asl_open_palm.canonical_description: Form a loose-thumb 'A' (or 'S') hand and lift it with the other hand; directional to indicate who is helping. (Lifeprint)

asl_thumb_up.canonical_description: Form a 'W' handshape and tap the index finger to the mouth twice. (Lifeprint)

asl_index_up.canonical_description: Tap the fingertips of the dominant 'bent' hand on the upturned wrist of the base hand (pulse area). (Lifeprint)

asl_index_middle_up.canonical_description: Touch the middle finger of the dominant hand to the palm of the other hand and pivot side-to-side. (Lifeprint)

asl_open_palm_spread.description: ASL-inspired open palm with wide finger spread
asl_open_palm_spread.canonical_description: Shake an 'E' handshape frantically from side to side to indicate 'emergency'. (Lifeprint)

asl_fist.canonical_description: Extend the index fingers of both hands and jab/twist them toward each other (or near the painful location). (Lifeprint)

asl_thumb_index_pinch.canonical_description: Use an 'S' (fist) handshape and nod the wrist up-and-down to mimic a head nod for 'yes'. (Lifeprint)

asl_index_pinky_up.canonical_description: Bring the index and middle fingers to the thumb (pinch motion) or use a small side-to-side motion; often accompanied by a headshake. (Lifeprint)

asl_stop_palm_no_thumb.description: ASL-inspired stop hand (four fingers up, thumb tucked)
asl_stop_palm_no_thumb.canonical_description: Extend one palm up and sharply bring the other open hand down to it at a right angle (chop). (Lifeprint)

asl_thumb_index_middle_up.description: ASL-inspired thumb, index and middle up
asl_thumb_index_middle_up.canonical_description: Start with a flat hand near the lips and move it forward and slightly down toward the person you're thanking. (Lifeprint)
